A slide deck receives the same compiled figure as any other format.
Three options apply to Reveal.js alone, so this page shows the source and describes the result.

::: {.callout-note}
This page is HTML, not a deck.
To see the options at work, render a Reveal.js document.
`example-render.tar.gz` on the [latest release](https://github.com/mcanouil/quarto-typst-render/releases/latest) carries one source rendered to Reveal.js and to Beamer.
:::

## Placing the output

`output-location` decides where the figure appears when the source is echoed beside it:

| Value | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `fragment` | The figure appears on a click, after the source. |
| `slide` | The figure moves to a slide of its own, which follows the source. |
| `column` | The source and the figure sit side by side. |
| `column-fragment` | The same two columns, with the figure revealed on a click. |

: Where a compiled figure lands on a slide. {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[26,74]"}

````markdown
```{typst}
//| echo: true
//| output-location: column
#circle(radius: 1.5cm, fill: blue.lighten(60%))
```
````

The option is ignored in every other format.

## Stepping through the source

`code-line-numbers` highlights lines of the echoed source.
A string steps through them, one step per `|`:

````markdown
```{typst}
//| echo: true
//| code-line-numbers: "1|2-3|4"
#set text(size: 14pt)
#let shape(fill) = circle(radius: 1cm, fill: fill)
#stack(dir: ltr, spacing: 1em, shape(blue), shape(orange))
#align(center)[Two shapes]
```
````

Each step highlights its lines as the speaker advances.
A range uses `-`, a set uses `,`, and `true` numbers the lines without stepping.
The option needs `echo: true`.

## Sizing a figure to the slide

`classes` adds CSS classes to the image element, so Reveal.js can size it:

````markdown
```{typst}
//| classes: r-stretch
#circle(radius: 4cm, fill: teal.lighten(60%))
```
````

`r-stretch` makes the figure take the free height of the slide.
Ask for `format: svg` in a deck, so the figure stays sharp on a projector:

```yaml
format: revealjs
extensions:
  typst-render:
    format: svg
```

## PowerPoint

Blocks work in PowerPoint as everywhere else.
An inline expression does not, because Pandoc cannot put an image inside a run of text there.
Move the expression into a block, or keep it for the other formats.
